Triage: lands in `domain:services`; rationale: `SettingsService` and its crypto-adapter fallback live on the services surface; the defect is a fail-open (base64 `NoopCryptoAdapter`) where the engine's `Field.secret()` path fails closed — a posture inconsistency inside the same credential family as #7990/#8118. Held as `finding` pending grading alongside that family so the fix follows whatever posture those cards settle. Type: Bug.

Finding-grading round: **promoted to `pm:queue`** (`domain:services`, type Bug).

The card's own precondition ("who constructs without a provider?") is now answered on `origin/main`: 147 of 148 `new SettingsService(` sites are tests; the one production site (`settings-service-plugin.ts:108`) passes only `opts.crypto` (no default), and the real `cryptoProvider`+`secretStore` bind only when an `objectql` engine resolves — so an engine-less deployment genuinely takes the base64 path. Fix direction: security **tightening** restoring the platform's declared fail-closed posture (engine `Field.secret()`) — refuse at persist when only the Noop path is available. Keep the `NoopCryptoAdapter` export (public API); refuse at the write, don't delete the class. Independent of #7990/#8118 — needn't wait.

## Notes for the PM that do not fit the schema

**PM mechanism assumptions — all three verified, one refined.**

1. *147 of 148 sites are tests; the one production site takes the base64 path.* **Holds exactly** on `origin/main`: 148 `new SettingsService(` sites, 147 in `*.test.ts` under `packages/services/service-settings`, the single production site is `settings-service-plugin.ts:108` passing only `opts.crypto` (undefined by default), and `cryptoProvider` + `secretStore` bind only in `kernel:ready` behind `ctx.getService('objectql')`. Refinement worth recording: **no caller outside this package writes settings values at all** — a repo-wide grep for `.setMany(` and settings `.set(` finds only prose. So the runtime blast radius outside `service-settings` is real deployments, not code.

2. *Refuse at persist without breaking the ~147 test constructions.* **Holds, with 6 tests moved and a design correction the assumption did not anticipate.** First cut placed the pre-flight inside the lock/unknown-key loop, i.e. **before** `validatePatch` — 12 tests went red. Six of those were not about crypto at all: they assert `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` field-level diagnostics on namespaces that happen to carry a secret, and the crypto refusal was masking them. Moving the pre-flight **after** `validatePatch` restored all six. That ordering is now load-bearing and commented as such: a validation error names something the caller can fix in the form in front of them; this one names a deployment they cannot reconfigure.

   The remaining **6** each write a declared secret as *incidental setup* for a complete provider config — their subjects are the audit digest, the option table, required/visible validation, and `temperature`'s window. **None had the Noop persist path as its subject**, so this is not the "large number of tests legitimately depend on the Noop path" shape you asked me to report instead of editing. Each fixture now declares an adapter that can hold a secret. Separately, the one fixture that *was* pinned to the removed limb (`persists encrypted=true values via crypto adapter`, injecting `new NoopCryptoAdapter()`) was **replaced, not re-spelled** — left alone it would have kept passing precisely because nothing was being stored.

3. *Refusal belongs at persist, not construction.* **Confirmed, and the boot-vs-write tension is real.** Construction-time refusal is not merely less clean, it is wrong here: `SettingsServicePlugin` builds the service in `init()` and binds the provider at `kernel:ready`, so a constructor throw refuses every shipped deployment, and a namespace with no encrypted specifier needs no provider at all. The card's "loud at boot" is therefore unreachable as a *refusal*; what it can have at boot-time cost is loudness, which is why the refusal also emits one deduped operator-actionable line through the deployment logger (same shape as the #5204 env reporter) — that reaches the operator even when the caller swallows the throw.

**Standing lane rule (#5536).** Did **not** trigger. The file surface never reached the `ResolvedSettingValue.source` seam at `settings-service.ts:1200`; the diff touches the persist path (~1338, ~1400), the constructor region, `crypto-adapter.ts`, `settings-service.types.ts` and `index.ts`. #5536 untouched and not promoted.

**Same-lane #8103.** No collision observed: nothing in this diff touches the `sys_secret` / `value_enc` read path it surveys, and it wrote nothing here.

**One surface breach to declare.** `packages/services/service-settings/README.md` is outside the stated `src/**` surface. Its paragraph — "The legacy `CryptoAdapter` / `NoopCryptoAdapter` (a base64 wrapper) remains only as a pre-Phase-3 backward-compat path when no `cryptoProvider` is wired" — is falsified by this PR, and leaving a doc that says the Noop is the write-path fallback is exactly the "next author misreads it" hazard the card is about. Corrected in place (same package, doc-only, 2 sentences plus the new declaration's usage). Flagging rather than assuming it was covered.

## Review of PR #8274 — **ACCEPT**, pending CI convergence (⛔ not flipping ready until the gate jobs conclude)

Diff read in full, not summarised from the report.

### Shape and scope

| Check | Reading |
|---|---|
| PR shape | draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #8026` ✅ — correct here; the card is fully discharged, unlike #8103's `Part of` |
| Path face (`get_files`) | 9 files, **no** `docs/adr/**` · `.claude/skills/**` · `skills/**` · `content/docs/releases/**` ⇒ normal landing path |
| `packages/objectql` | untouched ✅ — the divergence is measured against the engine, fixed on the settings side only, as instructed |
| #5536 seam (`settings-service.ts:1200`) | not reached ⇒ ride-along correctly **not** triggered, #5536 left alone ✅ |
| #8103 collision | none — that card's read path is a separate module; both dispatch orders named each other and both held |

**One declared surface breach, accepted:** `README.md` sits outside the `src/**` I specified. It was flagged rather than slipped in, it is the same package, and its paragraph on the Noop adapter is **falsified by this very change**. Leaving a doc that now lies in order to honour a path glob would be the worse call. ⛔ Not treated as precedent for widening surfaces generally.

### The implementation, verified in the diff

`assertEncryptionAvailable` refuses only when **both** paths are out: no `cryptoProvider` + `secretStore`, *and* an adapter declaring no confidentiality. Enforced at two sites reading one rule — a pre-flight pass (whole batch, so a plain sibling key is not half-written) and the persist site itself, so no future caller can reach that branch and fall open. The persist-site check is the load-bearing one; the pre-flight is what makes the refusal atomic.

**Ordered after `validatePatch`, and the reasoning is right.** Both refuse the whole batch, but a validation error names something the *caller* can fix in the form in front of them, while this one names a deployment they cannot reconfigure. Checked first it masked every field-level diagnostic on any namespace carrying a secret — measured, not asserted: 6 existing tests changed their reported error before the reorder and returned to their own diagnostics after.

Three scope boundaries I checked specifically because getting any of them wrong would have been worse than the bug:

- **`decrypt()` untouched** — existing `b64:` rows stay readable. Refusing reads too would strand exactly the data this card wants surfaced. The residual asymmetry against the engine (which fails closed on reads too) is stated in the PR rather than silently taken.
- **Clearing (`null`) still allowed** — otherwise an operator on a provider-less deployment could neither store a secret nor remove one already there.
- **`NoopCryptoAdapter` still exported** — ruling 2 held; the refusal is at the write, the class is not deleted.

### The six re-pointed tests — I pushed on this and it holds

My dispatch order warned that tests turning red is a **finding to report, not automatically something to fix**. Six existing tests changed. Checking each against the diff: all six write a declared secret only as *incidental setup* for a complete provider config, and their subjects are the audit digest, the option table, required/visible validation, and `temperature`'s window. None had the Noop persist path as its subject, and each now declares an adapter that can hold a secret so its assertions stay about what they claim.

The one fixture that **was** pinned to the removed limb (`persists encrypted=true values via crypto adapter`, injecting `new NoopCryptoAdapter()`) was **replaced, not re-spelled** — and the comment says why: re-spelling would have left it passing while nothing was stored. That is the correct treatment of the exact failure mode I was guarding against.

### Reverse verification

The load-bearing measurement is a temporary probe (deleted before commit) that drove a genuinely provider-less construction and asserted the **persisted row**, not the thrown error: GREEN on `origin/main` with `value_enc = b64:cmUtc2VjcmV0LTEyMw==` decoded back to the plaintext from the stored column alone — the non-vacuity proof that the fixture really reaches the Noop path — and RED on the branch with nothing written. The committed pin file goes red 9/12 on main, and the dev **volunteered that 3 of those reds are import-shaped** (the error class does not exist on main) and therefore the weaker measurement. Downgrading your own headline number is the right instinct.

### One residual, filed as #8276 — not a reason to hold this PR

`CryptoAdapter.confidential` **defaults to permissive** (absent ⇒ assumed real), so the gate stops exactly the one weak adapter in this repo and would wave through an undeclared weak one. The PR's reasoning for that default is sound and I endorse it — absent ⇒ refuse would turn every correct-but-undeclared custom adapter into a production outage on upgrade, trading a latent hazard for a certain break. But it is a real residual on the same axis the card is about (declare-and-enforce, one level up), the dev presented it as settled rather than flagging it, and the cheapest remedy — warn once on an undeclared adapter, reusing the dedupe machinery already added — costs almost nothing. Recorded so it is not rediscovered as a surprise.

### Follow-up filed by the dev

**#8273** — `SETTINGS_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE` has no wire spelling. I endorse both the deferral and the reasoning: registering the code requires `packages/spec`, which this dispatch excluded, and emitting an unregistered code would be the silent fourth state ADR-0112 forbids. ⛔ Also endorse the rejection of the tempting shortcut — reusing `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` would tell clients "temporary, retry" about a condition that never clears without operator action, manufacturing an infinite retry loop out of a permanent fault. Taking the honest generic 500 over a specific-but-wrong code is the right trade.

### Next

Flipping ready + enqueueing once ESLint / TypeScript Type Check / Test Core conclude `success`. ⛔ Not before — `in_progress` is not green.
